messages.author: e99a6e0ce88dcab6
messages.subject: Failed to fit, returning Error in fasthistoriescpp :  Error in function ibeta_derivative
parts:
Dear all,

After I have successfully run my codes on my PC couple times before transferring to my M1 Mac. I then believe the code should work fine, none of error so far until this model fitting. I have got this error while I trying to fit my data to a simple model:

LPRDfitEx2019 <- secr.fit(capthist=spatDetectHistLPRDidentified2019,
                      detectfn='EX',  buffer=10*initialsigma2019,  trace=FALSE )

I keep getting this error message: 
Error in fasthistoriescpp(as.integer(m), as.integer(nc), as.integer(nrow(realparval)), : Error in function ibeta_derivative<long double>(long double,long double,long double): Overflow Error
I have tried different method, i.e.  method="Newton-Raphson" , "BFGS", but none of this works.

I would greatly appreciate it if anyone could help.

Best regards,
Manoon

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Failed to fit, returning Error in fasthistoriescpp : Error in function ibeta_derivative
parts: I haven't seen that before, and can't imagine why it would differ between platforms. I guess there is something odd about your data to trigger this, so a summary would be helpful. Also what version are you using?  It seems ibeta_derivative is called internally by a Boost distribution function used by 'secr'. You might get around it by setting details = list(fastproximity = FALSE).Murray

messages.author: 23569cd64661cf9a
messages.subject: Re: Failed to fit, returning Error in fasthistoriescpp : Error in function ibeta_derivative
parts:
Hi all, 

I wanted to jump in and note that I was running into a similar error using secr on my MacBook Pro M1. I am using secr version 4.5.8. Some models ran, but others produced this error. It tended to show up more often when I estimated more parameters in the model, but overall it is unpredictable. 

For example, this model would run: 
m9W <- secr.fit(capthistW, model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~session), buffer = 10000, CL = FALSE, detectfn = 0, method = "Newton-Raphson")
But this model would produce an error:
m6W <- secr.fit(capthistW, model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~h2), buffer = 10000, CL = FALSE, detectfn = 0, method = "Newton-Raphson")

Following Murray's earlier suggestion, specifying details = list(fastproximity = FALSE) solved the problem. So luckily there is a workaround, but it did significantly increase the run time. Happy to provide more information if helpful. 

Best, 
Elizabeth
